transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, because I know it's probably a little silly... but I'm here because flying has just started to feel way scarier than it really should. 

Like, just the idea of getting on a plane makes me picture this bad turbulence we hit on my honeymoon flight, and I get all worked up. I know people fly safely every single day, and I know I shouldn't let it get to me... is it okay that I'm coming in for something like that? I just want to fix it so I'm not being difficult or holding up plans when we travel, if that makes sense?
Is it just flying that makes you feel anxious, or are there other situations that trigger similar feelings of fear or worry?

No, it's really just the flying. I mean, I don't love spiders or anything, but who does, right? But no, I don't get this worked up about anything else. I'm usually a pretty calm person, especially at work. I help run a daycare, so I have to be the steady one, you know? 

It's just... this one specific thing. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been avoiding flying or making significant changes to your travel plans because of this fear?

Um... well, I guess I have been, a little bit? I try really hard not to be an inconvenience to anyone, I promise. But... I have sort of been choosing long drives instead for our vacations. Which is fine, road trips are fun! But I did actually turn down a work training recently because I would have had to fly. I just told my boss the timing wasn't right, because I really didn't want to sound unprofessional or incapable... I hope that was okay to do. 

And, honestly, if I absolutely have to talk about planning a trip, I kind of need my husband sitting right there with me to get through the conversation without backing out of it completely. I know that probably sounds so silly for a grown woman to say... I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? Does that make sense?
How often do you find yourself thinking about or worrying about flying when you're not actually planning a trip?

Um, honestly, not really at all. When I'm not actively planning a trip or, you know, having to think about getting on a plane, it really doesn't cross my mind. I'm usually just so busy with the kids at work, and life in general, that I don't really have time to dwell on it. 

I guess I only really get that nervous feeling when it's right in front of me, like when we're trying to figure out vacation plans or if someone brings up booking a flight. Otherwise, I'm totally fine! I hope that's a good thing? Like, it means it's not too serious, right?
How would you rate your level of anxiety when you are on a plane or thinking about flying?

Um, on a scale? I guess... maybe a little high? But I really try not to let it show too much. I don't want to make a scene or bother the people around me, you know? 

But, um, honestly, if I'm even just looking at flights on my laptop for a conference, or... or even if I just hear a plane flying overhead while I'm outside, my chest just gets so tight, like, instantly. I get this sudden rush of panic, and I just feel this overwhelming urge to slam my laptop shut or just... get away from whatever is making me think about it. 

It passes, though! I promise I don't stay like that all day. It's just that initial reaction. Is... is that normal for people who don't like flying? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting or being too dramatic about it.
Has your fear of flying affected your relationships with family or friends in any way?

Um, I think my relationships are mostly okay? I mean, I try really hard not to let it affect my family or my friends. I'm still doing everything I need to do at work, and I keep up with everything at home with my husband. I really don't want to be a burden on anyone. 

But... well, I guess it has affected a few things, if I'm being completely honest. Like I mentioned, I've been passing up on those work trainings and conferences. My supervisor really thinks they'd help me grow, and I just hate letting her down... I always make up an excuse so she doesn't think I'm just slacking off. 

And, um, it has pushed back some personal plans, too. Like, my husband and I had been talking about this trip to Florence that I was so excited about, but... I just keep finding reasons to delay booking it. He's been really patient, but I feel terrible that my silly fear is holding us back from doing fun things. I just want to be a good wife and a good employee, you know? Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too difficult.
Have you ever avoided social or professional events because they involved flying?

Um, well... I guess I kind of just touched on that, didn't I? I hope I'm answering these right. 

But, yes, I suppose I have avoided some things. Like those work trainings I mentioned... I just, I feel so bad turning them down, but I usually tell my boss I can't go because of childcare or scheduling conflicts. I don't want her to think I'm not dedicated! I really am. I just... I'd rather drive a really long way if I can, instead of flying. Like, if it's within driving distance, I'll totally go! I'll drive ten hours if I have to. 

And, um, if I absolutely have to sit down and talk about booking a flight, like for that trip to Florence... I really can't do it alone. I have to have my husband sitting right there next to me, just to kind of hold my hand and help me get through it so I don't just completely back out. He's so sweet about it, but I always feel a little embarrassed that I need him there just to look at a travel website. 

Is that... is it okay that I do that? Like, finding workarounds? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way.
Do you experience any physical symptoms, such as a racing heart or sweating, when you think about flying or are on a plane?

Um, physical symptoms? I... I don't really think so. I mean, maybe a little bit, but nothing too crazy, I promise. 

I know I mentioned my chest getting tight earlier, but it's not like I'm having a full-blown heart attack or sweating through my clothes or anything like that. I try really hard to keep it together. I guess sometimes my heart might beat a little faster if I'm really stressed about it, but I just take some deep breaths and try to calm myself down so I don't bother anyone. 

I don't usually get sweaty or dizzy or anything like that. I really hope that means it's not too serious? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I explaining that okay?
Have you ever turned down a significant opportunity, such as a dream job or a unique experience, because it required flying?

Um, well... I guess, like I was saying before, I have turned down those work trainings. I really don't want to call them a "dream job" opportunity or anything huge like that, because I don't want to sound like I'm ruining my life over this. I'm still doing really well at my job, I promise! I manage everything I need to do. 

But... yeah, my supervisor did say those conferences would be really good for my growth, and I just keep finding ways out of them. And, um, I guess that Florence trip is a pretty unique experience that I've been putting off. I just feel so bad that I'm letting these things slide, but I really am trying my best to keep everything else running smoothly at home and at work. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too incapable? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job with everything else, even if I struggle with this one little thing. Am I making sense?
How long have you been experiencing this fear of flying?

Um, let's see... I guess it's been a little while now. Not my whole life, I promise! I used to be totally fine with flying. 

But, um, it really started after my honeymoon. We had this one flight back that was just... well, it was really bumpy. A lot of turbulence. I'm sure the pilots had it completely under control, but it just really shook me up for some reason. 

That was about two years and five months ago. So, I guess it's been going on since then. But I've been managing! I mean, two and a half years isn't that long in the grand scheme of things, right? I'm really hoping it's just a phase and I'll snap out of it soon. Does that timeline seem pretty normal to you?
Have you avoided any important life events, such as weddings or funerals, because they required flying?

Um, important life events? No, no, I haven't missed any weddings or funerals or anything like that. I would never want to let my family or friends down, I promise. I always make sure to be there for the big things. 

I mean, I guess I have been avoiding flying for them, though. Like, if we have to go somewhere, I'll just choose to drive instead, even if it's a really long drive. I don't mind the driving, really! It gives my husband and me time to talk. And, um, like I mentioned before, I have been turning down those work trainings. 

But I try not to let it ruin everything. It's just... if I absolutely have to even talk about a trip or plan one, I kind of need my husband sitting right there with me. Just to help me get through it without backing out entirely. I know that sounds a little silly, needing him just to talk about it, but it helps me stay on track so I don't let anyone down. I hope that doesn't make me sound too dependent? I really am trying to handle it the best I can.
Have you ever felt like your fear of flying has controlled your decisions to the point where you've avoided things you really wanted to do?

Um... well, like I was saying a little bit earlier, I really wouldn't say it completely controls me. That sounds so... so severe, you know? I’m still managing my job and my home life really well, I promise! I don't want you to think everything is just falling apart, because I'm definitely keeping up with my responsibilities. 

But... I guess, if I'm being really honest, it has made me avoid some things I'd normally jump at. Like I mentioned, I’ve started passing up those trainings and conferences that my supervisor thinks would help me grow at work. And... it just keeps pushing back our personal plans, too, like that Florence trip I’d been so, so excited about. 

I hate admitting that, because I feel like I should be stronger than this. It doesn't make me a total failure, does it? I really am trying to push through, I just hope it's normal to struggle with this kind of thing a little bit.
Have you ever felt like you're missing out on significant experiences or opportunities because of your fear of flying?

Um, well... I guess that's kind of similar to what we were just talking about, isn't it? I really don't want to sound like a broken record, or like I'm just complaining! 

But, um, yeah, I suppose I am missing out on a few things. Like I said, I'm still doing a really good job at work and keeping everything at home running smoothly—I promise I'm not letting anything important slide! But... it is true that I've been turning down those work trainings and conferences. My supervisor really thinks they'd be great for my career, and I just... I keep finding excuses not to go because they require a flight. 

And then there's the personal stuff. My husband and I were supposed to go to Florence, and I was so, so excited to see the art and the architecture, but we just keep pushing it back. I just can't bring myself to book the tickets. 

I feel terrible about it, honestly. I know I should just get on the plane and go. I'm not a bad employee or a bad wife for letting this hold me back a little, am I? I'm really hoping we can fix this so I can stop missing out on these things.
